title: The (R)evolution of Scientific Workflows in the Agentic AI Era: Towards Autonomous Science
problem: Modern scientific discovery requires coordinating distributed facilities and heterogeneous resources. Researchers act as manual workflow coordinators rather than scientists, limiting discovery velocity and scalability.
motivation: AI agents can provide intelligence within scientific workflow ecosystems to automate coordination, resource optimization, and decision-making, potentially accelerating discovery by 100x.
method: Propose a conceptual framework charting workflow evolution along two dimensions: intelligence (static to intelligent) and composition (single to swarm). Present architectural blueprint for autonomous, distributed scientific laboratories.
key_novelty: Conceptual framework for agentic AI integration into scientific workflows; evolutionary trajectory from current systems to fully autonomous science platforms.
contributions: Conceptual framework for AI agent integration in scientific workflows
Two-dimensional evolution model: intelligence and composition dimensions
Architectural blueprint for autonomous distributed scientific labs
Vision for 100x discovery acceleration through workflow automation
limitations: Conceptual framework paper with limited implementation details; technical feasibility and specific AI methodologies not detailed; scalability of autonomous systems unclear.
